en: Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Of this mantra of the Śrī Śāligrāma Stotra, the Blessed Lord is the Seer (ṛṣi), Nārāyaṇa is the Deity (devatā), Anuṣṭubh is the Meter (chandaḥ), and its application (viniyoga) is in the recitation of the Śrī Śāligrāma Stotra mantra.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
O Śrī Devadeva, Lord of gods, I wish to hear all about that supreme worship of the deities; tell it to me, O Puruṣottama.
The Blessed Lord said:
On the northern bank of the Gaṇḍakī and to the south of the King of Mountains lies the ground of a great sacred field, ten yojanas in extent. (2)
The Śāligrāma shall be the Lord, and Dvārāvatī shall be the Goddess;
where there is a union of both, liberation occurs there—of this there is no doubt. (3)
Wherever there is a Śāligrāma stone and wherever there is a Dvārāvatī stone, where these two meet, there is liberation; of this there is no doubt. (4)
Salutations to you, the water of the Śāligrāma stone, which removes all sins; to you who grants atonement for those who desire it for the misdeeds committed since birth. 5.
Having drunk the water from the feet of Viṣṇu, which removes untimely death and destroys all diseases, I bear it upon my head. 6.
Water placed within a conch shell and whirled over Keśava, when it adheres to the limbs of men, shall burn away even the sin of killing a Brahmin and other such evils. (7)
One should always drink the water used for bathing that has arisen from a stone marked with the discus;
having washed it so that the water is pure, it removes even the sin of killing a Brahmin. (8)
By consuming the food offering (naivedya) of Viṣṇu, one obtains the full fruit of thousands of Agniṣṭoma sacrifices and hundreds of Vājapeya sacrifices.

He who daily eats tulasī leaves mixed with the food offering (naivedya) and especially with the water from the feet of Viṣṇu before Murāri, obtains the merit of ten million times ten million sacrifices. || 10 ||
Whether they be broken, cracked, split, or even scorched by fire—wherever there is a Śāligrāma stone, no fault is found therein. (11)

In the worship of the Śāligrāma stone, there is no need for mantras, nor indeed for ritual offerings, nor pilgrimage sites, nor meditative cultivation; neither is there praise nor formal ceremonial service. (12)
Sins such as the killing of a Brahmin, arising from mind, speech, and body—all of these perish quickly through the worship of the Śāligrāma stone. (13)
Consisting of various colors and surrounded by manifold enjoyments, I shall likewise describe him who is beloved by Lakṣmī through the grace of the boon. (14)
I shall describe the God who is born from Nārāyaṇa, who by his own action resides within the discus, and likewise through the grace of his boon, is the beloved of Lakṣmī. (15)
On that black stone surface where a subtle discus is seen, one attains good fortune and progeny, and it bestows all happiness. (16)
Upon seeing the marks of Vāsudeva, one is liberated from sins;
Śrīdhara is seen on the left hand, being green in color. (17)
One should see there the god in the form of a boar, marked even with the limbs of a tortoise;
likewise, the footprint of Varāha and that of Vāmana should be seen there. (18)
The yellow-colored form belongs to the gods, while the red-colored one is terrifying; the Lord as Nṛsiṃha is proclaimed to be the bestower of liberation. (19)
The conch, discus, mace, and tortoise; wherever the conch is seen, that is the characteristic of the white-colored deity on the left side of the Lord. 20.
Likewise, Dāmodara is thick, with a wheel established in the middle;
it appears as a yellow line, constricted at the full gateway. (21)
If it is shaped like an umbrella, there will be sovereignty; if circular, great prosperity; if flat, great suffering; and if like the point of a spear, war is certain. (22)
The serpent Śeṣa upon the forehead and a beautiful golden crest above the head—these are the characteristics of Vāmadeva, who is the color of gold and a discus. (23)
And on the left side, indeed, there is a discus; [the deity] is dark-complexioned with tawny hair.
The deities Lakṣmī and Nṛsiṃha are seen to have distinct colors. (24)
If the lips are long, one will be poor; if they are tawny, there is only loss.
If the *lagna-cakra* is present, there will be disease; if it is torn, death is certain. (25)

One should always wear on one's head the water used for washing the feet and the floral remains (nirmālya) of Viṣṇu; and that which has been seen by Viṣṇu should be eaten, mixed with a leaf of Tulasī. 26.
One who possesses even a single drop of water from a Śāligrāma stone dwells eternally in Vaikuṇṭha for thousands of millions of kalpas; such a drop destroys ten million murders. (27)
Therefore, one should always worship [it] after meditating upon it, and likewise that which has been worshipped;
and the best of the twice-born who recites this hymn to the Śāligrāma stone—28.
He shall go to that supreme abode where Hari, the Lord of the World, resides;
liberated from all sins, he goes to the world of Viṣṇu. (29)
The ten incarnations of the gods are seen to have distinct colors;
by worshipping Viṣṇu in due order, one obtains the desired kingdom. (30)
Indeed, millions of sins of killing a Brahmin and millions of sins of approaching those who should not be approached—all these go to destruction by eating the food offered to Viṣṇu. (31)
Having drunk the water from Viṣṇu’s feet, which destroys the sins of ten million births, one incurs eight times that sin by letting even a single drop fall upon the ground. (32)
Thus ends the Śāligrāma Stotra in the glorious Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa, within the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira.
